# NOTES: "Cities in the Air" by Edmond Hamilton (Air Wonder Stories, Nov/Dec 1929; Gutenberg #74171)

(Single book, no BOOK headings. Chapters I–XI plus untitled "Dawnward"/"The End". Preface blurb by editors praises audacity; notes air-cities and high-altitude health.)

## Setting / World
- Narrator: Captain Martin Brant, American Federation Air-Cruiser 3885. First officer: Macklin. Second officer: Hilliard (young).
- Three Federations: American (North/South America, capital New York); European (Europe west of Caucasus + Africa, capital Berlin); Asiatic (Asia + Australasia, capital Peking).
- Third Air War 2039 ~30 yrs before. Cruisers power from atmospheric/electrostatic charge via transformers; tube-propellers (horizontal = forward, vertical = lift). Speed ~1000 mph. Cruisers submerge (liquid-air tanks, water-propulsion).
- Air-forts: domed cubes 500 ft wide, 5 miles up, rings 5 miles apart; held aloft by cosmic-ray gravity repulsion; dynamic towers collect energy.
- Air-cities: circular metal disks, base >1000 ft thick, 5 miles diameter, towers to 5000 ft more; 5 miles up (~4 miles some). Central electrostatic power-tower/pinnacle. Named after old Earth cities (New York, Berlin, Peking, Tokio, Chicago, San Francisco, Buenos Aires, London, Paris, etc.). American: 100 cities, ~5M people each. European+Asiatic: 200 cities.
- Weapons: heat-guns; heat-shells (radiant heat, burst in blinding flare); heat-bombs; heat-pistols (hand weapon, heat-cartridges); cruiser-finders (cone-shaped, detect electrostatic motors); air-mines (floating cube containers of heat charge).
- Control room: six direction-levers + speed-knob; table-map with red circles for cities (projectors from cruiser-finder batteries); six glass periscope screens (one above, one below, four sides); distance-phone (communication); order-phone.
- Vibration-locks open doors by frequency. Food: synthetic paste.

## Chapter I: On to New York
- Distance-phone order from First Air Chief: European + Asiatic Federations allied; European fleet 5000 cruisers racing over Atlantic toward New York; Asiatic 5000 over Pacific toward western coast. Macklin turns cruiser east at full speed.
- Pass over Alleghanies, Appalachians; air-forts (line 5 miles apart).
- New York: five-mile floating city; New York of earth was on narrow island. Land below deserted.
- Landing at central plaza; First Air Chief Yarnall with squadron commanders. Yarnall's speech: battle must not be lost; Central Council orders; Second Air Chief commands western fleet from San Francisco. Air-forts moved east of city. City moves inland. "Last Air War begins." Yarnall's flagship has three parallel silver stripes.

## Chapter II: Battle Over the Atlantic
- Fleet speed 800 mph. Squadrons 1–6 scout. Brant's squadron 1 (200 ships) meets 500 European scouts. Collision; heat-shells; cruisers plunge.
- European ring formation; Brant's fleet splits, passes both sides, hits with heat-shells. European double-file splits Brant's columns. Brant's column encircled. Yarnall orders "Triangle formation! North at full speed!" Triangle smashes through. Reunited fleet forms rectangle.
- Both fleets dive into Atlantic depths.

## Chapter III: Under the Sea
- Undersea battle; Hilliard warns walls are searing. Gunners concentrate on enemy column head (Yarnall's maneuver). Fleets surface, mid-air deadlock.
- Yarnall: "Retreat-formation! All ships retreat westward at full speed!" T-formation. Flee toward air-forts.

## Chapter IV (cont. in V)... Chapter III cont: Into the Clouds; The Ambush
- Air-forts vanished; Yarnall leads fleet into cloud-bank (artificial vapor from air-forts). Drop order: "All American Federation ships—drop!" Clouds dispersed by air-jets; air-forts' heat-guns destroy trapped European fleet. European fleet flees east (~2000 left).

## Chapter III: Homeward (Yarnall speech)
- Second Air Chief from San Francisco also won by cloud-ambush over Asiatic fleet. Yarnall: respite only; enemy can build cruisers faster. Fleet returns to New York.

## Chapter IV: A Desperate Plan (The Respite Ended)
- Yarnall (in tower): European/Asiatic preparing secret weapon at Berlin and Peking. Plan: raid Berlin (Brant commands 250 cruisers); San Francisco raids Peking. 
- Sail east over Atlantic; avoid detection by faking westward heading. Triangle formation. Cruisers fly 8 miles high.

## Chapter IV (cont.): Above the Enemy
- Patrol ring crosses; Brant warns, cruisers slow. Second patrol sees them; 80 American cruisers ram 20 patrol-cruisers; 25 American and all 20 enemy fall; 55 survive.
- Air-fort chain (double line) at western European approaches; mine-field in vapor layer; creep through using cruiser-finders (Hilliard reports mines). Escape above.
- Pass London (southwest England) and Paris (lights) at high altitude. Berlin seen: circle as large as New York, 4 miles high, central electrostatic tower.

## Chapter IV (cont.): A Sudden Attack
- Brant orders dive; heat-bombs released from bomb-slots (rows of white buttons). Eastern arsenals and cruisers destroyed (~500 cruisers, fused craters). Second swoop on western arsenals. Patrols chase.
- Two patrol cruisers ram Brant's cruiser from above; Brant's cruiser (and two enemy cruisers) crash. Brant, Macklin, Hilliard survive in bridge-room; rest of crew dies.

## Chapter V: Captured
- Brant's cruiser fell onto Berlin street. Captured by green-uniformed European guards. Control room of Berlin tower. European First Air Chief (swarthy, black-haired, black probing eyes, five metal wing insignia) questions them. Threatens: fortnight, then "unpleasant procedures." Cell on 100th story.
- Cell mate: Connell (former cruiser captain, friend of Brant; sent a year earlier by First Air Chief to spy). Connell's story: worked way into European fleet via motor section (eight months). Learned that European/Asiatic air-cities would use new horizontal tube-propellers (many smaller tubes drawing air from different directions) allowing hundreds of mph. Captured trying to escape after forged document detected. Refused to reveal fellow agents. Attack planned in ~fortnight.
- Cell window faces plaza ~1000 ft below; no escape seemed possible. Days pass; Hilliard devises plan.

## Chapter VI: A Daring Venture
- Plan: overpower two food-guards at dusk; Macklin imitates a guard; disguise in green uniforms. Macklin and Connell escape in cruiser (Brant and Hilliard stay). Cruiser fired on by Berlin batteries; apparently destroyed in flare, falls.
- Brant: "back home with Connell, for God's sake!" (yelled to Macklin).

## Chapter VII: The Great Movement Starts
- Two days from attack; eighth day after escape. Berlin moves west at 100-150 mph. Gathering of cities: London, Stockholm, Geneva, Rome, Paris, Brussels, Amsterdam, Moscow, Helsingfors, Leningrad; over 100 cities gather around Berlin.
- Hilliard and Brant cut bunk-racks' metal strips (angles), make leather-belt ropes; plan descent.

## Chapter VIII: A Single Chance
- Brant and Hilliard slide down tower's window-line on metal angles and leather ropes. Alarm raised; they escape in unguarded cruiser from plaza; flee west. Hilliard reports all hundred European cities moving west. Pursued by ~100 cruisers; Brant dives through vapor layer twice; trapped. Ambush rescued by American cruisers (Macklin's). Macklin's cruiser faked its destruction (shells from its own gun detonated enemy shells). Macklin reveals Connell got back with secret; American cities prepared with new tube-propellers in ten days.

## Chapter IX: The Battle of the Air-Cities
- American cities (100) massed south of Great Lakes around New York; Boston, Los Angeles, Rio de Janeiro, Chicago, Mexico City, Quebec, Valparaiso, Miami, etc.
- Brant placed at New York controls; Macklin and Hilliard stay in control room; Connell in distance-phone position; Yarnall center. Six periscope screens. Map shows enemy armadas (east: European; west: Asiatic).
- Cruiser fleets clash; American cloud-projectors used again. Paris and Lisbon destroyed (east); Omaha destroyed (west).

## Chapter X: The First Clash / Armageddon
- Cities: Hong-Kong, New Orleans, St. Louis, Miami, Seattle, Singapore, Colombo, Brussels, Moscow, Shanghai, Algiers, etc. Enemy form crescents to encircle; New York moves north at full speed; crash through gap, shearing Moscow, Shanghai, Sydney, Algiers, Boston, Detroit, etc.

## Chapter XI: City Against City
- New York vs. Peking duel; Chicago vs. London (London falls). Enemy encircles American cities; American cities drop to ~60, then ~50. Yarnall: "They've got us!" Brant's plan: hundred cruisers in plaza. Brant, Macklin, Connell, Hilliard, with ~150 men, board cruisers; storm tower on five levels; kill guards; capture Berlin tower control room, killing European First Air Chief and two officers.
- Brant takes Berlin controls: moves into Geneva (Geneva falls), Stockholm, Cape Town, Bucharest fall. Peking destroyed by Berlin. Remaining enemy cities destroyed by Berlin. Brant drives Berlin into the earth (Berlin destroyed) after tearing lever off; Brant's group escapes via windows in cruisers.
- Dawn: American cities separate; Washington, Pittsburgh, Guatemala, Tacoma, Chicago, Philadelphia, Rio de Janeiro, Kansas City, Vancouver leave. Yarnall: two-thirds of world's cities destroyed, half of ours. Macklin: "Earth's Last Air War." Brant takes New York east toward sunrise. Final line: "It was the sun rising on a world at peace."

## Key Names (summary)
Martin Brant (narrator, captain); Macklin (first officer); Hilliard (second officer); Yarnall (First Air Chief, American); Connell (ex-cruiser captain, spy); Second Air Chief (San Francisco, unnamed); European First Air Chief (unnamed, swarthy, black eyes).
